2023_078_hs_cdb_23_24.paragraph: The 2023-2024 Course Descriptions book for Athens High School and Troy High School, revised January 2023 and issued under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, catalogs the credit-bearing courses offered at Troy School District's two comprehensive high schools together with graduation requirements, the district nondiscrimination policy, and the Oakland Schools Technical Campus option. Graduation requires 22.5 total credits, of which 18.50 are specified required credits spanning English, mathematics, science, social studies, physical education, health, world language/fine and applied arts/CTE, plus a non-credit 20-hour online learning experience.
2023_078_hs_cdb_23_24.page:
Publication
Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School, 2023-2024, Troy School District; revised January 2023; Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Athens High School: Dr. Lara Dixon, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085 (main 248.823.2900, fax 248.823.2913, counseling 248.823.2962, attendance 248.823.2901). Troy High School: Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098 (main 248.823.2700, fax 248.823.2713, counseling 248.823.2715, attendance 248.823.2701). Back matter lists the Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221.

Nondiscrimination
The policy statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is the Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, at 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248) 823-4000. The Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students.

Graduation requirements (Class of 2023 and beyond)

| Department | Required credits |
| --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE | 3.0 |
| Online Learning | 0.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Total Required Credits | 18.50 |
| Total Credits Needed for Graduation | 22.5 |

English comprises English 9 (1.0 credit, beginning with the class of 2027), English 10 Lit/Comp 1 & 2, English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2, and English 12 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 or 12 English AP 1 & 2. Science for the class of 2027 is Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5/Physics 0.5, and Earth Science 0.5/Science Elective 0.5; for the classes of 2024, 2025 and 2026 it is Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0, and a Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics is Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 (or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B, or CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a math elective, each 1.0 credit; four math credits must be earned while enrolled in high school and at least 1.0 credit of math or a math-related course must be completed in the final year. Social Studies is World History/Geography 1 & 2, American History/Geography 1 & 2, Economics 0.5, and Government and Civics 0.5. Physical Education is Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 plus a P.E. elective 0.5. A separate 1.0 credit of VPAA is noted, covering Industrial Technology, Business and Life Skills classes. The world language block requires 2.0 credits of world language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 credit of world language plus 1.0 credit of CTE or VPAA. Online learning is a 20-hour non-credit requirement embedded in Troy classes. State assessment requirements may be waived for the classes of 2021 and 2022.

Flexibility options (Class of 2016 and beyond, updated 9.2015, MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b)
Personal Curriculum aligned to a student's Educational Development Plan; excusal from the 0.5 P.E. elective for two seasons of district athletics or two seasons of marching band, tracked automatically; world language flexibility for heritage proficiency, international study and residence, or substitution of CTE or VPAA credits; and CTE program completion exchanged 1:1 for required science, world language, or Algebra 2 credit.

Course catalog
Departments covered include Business (Accounting and Finance, Business Management, Marketing), Career Technical Education (Education Occupations, Hospitality/Food Services, Automotive, Woodworking, Mechatronics), Industrial Technical, Life Skills, English, English Language Development, Fine Arts (Visual Arts, Music, Theatre Arts), Health, Mathematics, Media, Multi-Departmental, Physical Education, Science, Social Studies, Special Education, and World Language (French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese, German). Each listing gives a course number, grade levels, length and credit, retake rules, and prerequisites; a course with no school named is offered at both high schools.

Oakland Schools Technical Campus
OSTC-Southeast, 5055 Delemere Street (north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge), Royal Oak, serves grades 11-12 in two sessions, 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM. Credits are generally 1.5 per semester; OSTC credits are not NCAA approved. Applications are made online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February.

Grievance procedure
The antidiscrimination grievance procedure runs three steps through the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services and then the Superintendent, whose written answer is final and binding.

Publication and school contacts. The 2023-2024 Course Descriptions book covers Athens High School and Troy High School in the Troy School District, was revised January 2023, and carries the name of Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Athens High School is led by Principal Dr. Lara Dixon at 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085, with a main office number of 248.823.2900, fax 248.823.2913, counseling 248.823.2962, and attendance 248.823.2901. Troy High School is led by Principal Mr. Remo Roncone at 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098, with a main office number of 248.823.2700, fax 248.823.2713, counseling 248.823.2715, and attendance 248.823.2701. The closing page lists the Department of Teaching & Learning at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221, and the Special Education section directs inquiries to Central Office Special Education at 248.823.5096.

Nondiscrimination policy. The opening statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is the appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, reachable at Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248) 823-4000; the District's Director of Special Education has been appointed Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Grievance forms are available through any school office, and bargaining-unit employees may alternatively use the grievance procedure in their collective bargaining agreement.

Graduation requirements, Class of 2023 and beyond. English requires 4.0 credits: English 9 for 1.0 credit beginning with the class of 2027, English 10 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 for 1.0 credit, English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2 for 1.0 credit, and English 12 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 or 12 English AP 1 & 2 for 1.0 credit. Science requires 3.0 credits, with class of 2027 requirements of Biology 1.0 credit, Chemistry 0.5 credit/Physics 0.5 credit, and Earth Science 0.5 credit/Science Elective 0.5 credit; the current requirements for the classes of 2024, 2025 and 2026 are Biology 1.0 credit, Chemistry or Physics 1.0 credit, and Science Elective 1.0 credit. Mathematics requires 4.0 credits: Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B (which may also be met through CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a math elective, each 1.0 credit. High school math credits may be earned through a Troy middle school, but four credits of math must be earned while enrolled in high school, and at least 1.0 credit of math or a math-related course must be completed during the final year. Social Studies requires 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1 & 2 for 1.0, American History/Geography 1 & 2 for 1.0, Economics 0.5, and Government and Civics 0.5. Physical Education requires 1.0 credit through Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 and a P.E. elective 0.5. Health requires 0.5 credit. A 1.0 credit VPAA requirement covers Industrial Technology, Business and Life Skills classes. The World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE block requires 3.0 credits, satisfied by 2.0 credits of world language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 credit of world language plus either 1.0 credit of Career Technical Education or 1.0 credit of Visual, Performing or Applied Arts. Online Learning carries 0.0 credit but requires a 20-hour on-line learning experience embedded in Troy classroom experiences across middle and high school. State Assessments carry 0.0 credit and require completion of State of Michigan required assessments administered during high school; state assessment requirements may be waived for the classes of 2021 and 2022. Total required credits are 18.50 and total credits needed for graduation are 22.5. Credit-bearing high school courses taken before high school matriculation appear on the Troy transcript with grades earned, and high school courses may be retaken prior to or concurrent with the next course in a sequence, the retaken grade replacing the initial grade absent prior administrative approval.

Graduation requirement flexibility options, Class of 2016 and beyond, updated 9.2015, citing MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b. A Personal Curriculum permits additional core academic credits in lieu of other requirements when aligned to the student's Educational Development Plan. Students participating in two seasons of Troy School District athletics or two seasons of marching band are excused from the 0.5 credit physical education elective, tracked by an automated process with no forms required. The 2.0 credit world language requirement offers flexibility for non-English heritage language proficiency, international study and residence proficiency, and substitution of CTE or Visual & Performing or Applied Arts credits, documented through a Personal Curriculum. CTE program completion allows credits to be exchanged 1:1 for required science or world language credits, or to satisfy Algebra 2 when Algebra 2 content is embedded.

Business Department. Accounting and Finance includes 005002 Accounting 1, 005022 Accounting 2, and 005122 Financial Management, each one semester and one-half credit, and each satisfying one-half credit of the math-related graduation requirement in the 12th grade year. Business & Personal Law 1 (005052) and Business & Personal Law 2 (005062, Troy High) may be taken in any order. Business Management offerings include 005242 Business Management and Technology and 005232 Business Entrepreneurship. Junior Business Internship Co-op (105024/205024) requires 10 or more accumulated credits for junior status and Senior Business Internship Co-op (108844/208844) requires 14.5 or more credits for senior status, awarding up to 2.0 credits for work experience of at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester. Web Creation 1 (005272) and Web Page Creation 2 (005282) use the CS3 suite. Marketing includes 005222 Marketing 1, 005252 Marketing 2: Sales & Social Media Marketing, 005223 Honors Marketing (which prepares students for the Principles of Marketing CLEP examination), 005182 Sports and Entertainment Marketing with a Troy Athens Fantasy League, 005113 School-Based Enterprise for 12th grade only, and 005214 Marketing Internship Co-Op with 2 credit potential.

Career Technical Education. Careers in Education 1 (007393, Athens) and Careers in Education 2 (007403, Athens) use the Troy Athens Preschool; advanced placement credits are offered at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College and Davenport University, students may earn a Paraprofessional Certificate, and completing both courses qualifies students for the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Food services courses operate the renovated Terrace Café restaurant lab and use the ProStart curriculum, with the ServSafe Sanitation Certificate available: 007384 Restaurant Operations/Terrace Cafe (Athens, 2 hours, 2 credits), 007373 Commercial Baking (Athens), and 007473 Commercial Foods (Athens). Automotive offerings at Troy High are 007003 Automotive Technology 1, 007294 Automotive Tech 2 (a 2-hour block class requiring a C or better in Automotive Technology 1), 007213 Automotive Technology 3 and 007413 Automotive Technology 4; instruction meets NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards. Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2 and 3 are 007163, 007173 and 007183. Mechatronics 1 A & B (108713/208713) and Mechatronics 2 A & B (108723/208723) cover CAD, CAM, CNC and 3D printing.

Industrial Technical, Life Skills and Media. Architectural Drawing 1 (007072) and 2 (007082), Game Design 1 (007122, Athens) and 2 (007102, Athens) taught primarily in Java, and Introduction to Animation (007142) using 3DsMax. Life Skills includes 007242 Parenthood/Child Development 1 and 007262 Parenthood/Child Development 2, both eligible for advanced placement credit at Oakland Community College, 009862 Essential Skills for Adulthood, 007272 Personal Money Management, 007292 Foods and Culture (Troy High), 007282 Foods 2 (Troy High), 007332 Fashion Design 1 and 007342 Fashion Design 2 (Troy High), 007372 Stitchery (Troy High), and 007283 Interior Design (Troy High) using AutoCAD. Media offerings are 008492 Media Center Services and 008502 Media Center Techniques, plus 008682 Innovation Learning and 008692 Innovation Lab, influenced by the D school at Stanford University with references to creatinginnovators.com and dschool.stanford.edu.

English and ELD. Course numbers include 100063 and 200063 for 10 English Literature/Composition 1 and 2, 100073 and 200073 for the honors sections, 000082 for 11 English Literature/Composition, 100443 and 200443 for 11 English AP 1 and 2, 000113 for 12 English Lit/Comp, and 000453 for 12 English AP 1 & 2. Electives include Creative Writing 1 and 2 (000182, 000192), Classical Mythology and Drama (000232), Film and Literature (000212), Literature of Suspense (000312), Science Fiction (000382), Voices in Literature (000132), Sports Literature (000322), Personal Communication (000352), Speech 1 and 2 (000392, 000142), Debate 1 and 2 (000492, 000502), Modern Shakespeare (000242), Writing for Publication: Journalism (100273/200273), Newspaper (000333) and Yearbook (000343), Writing for Broadcasting (000342), Advanced Writing for Broadcasting (000362), and Advanced Publication Production (000353). Seminar AP and Research AP (002523 and 002533) culminate in an academic paper of approximately 4000-5000 words with an oral defense. English Language Development placement uses the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol and annual WIDA Access administration; courses include Beginner ELD (101013/20103), Intermediate ELD (101023/201023), Advanced ELD (101033/201033), Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs (101113/201113) and EL Tutorial (101103/201103), with language support content classes such as LS Biology (104703/204703), LS Introductory Physics (004313), LS World History/Geography 1 and 2 (002272, 002282), LS American History/Geography 1 and 2 (102703, 202703), LS Government/Civics (002092), LS Economics (002422) and LS Health (008862) rotating by school year.

Fine Arts, Health and Physical Education. Visual arts run from Multi-Media Art (006212), Mindful Art, Drawing 1 (006232) and Advanced Drawing (006243) through Painting (006252, 006263), Cartoons, Comics & Animation (006352), Ceramics (006272, 006283), Lettering & Calligraphy (006362), Studio Art (006373), Advanced Art AP (006393), Applied Arts and Design (006222), Computer Graphics (006422, 006433), Sculpture (006292), Principles of Photography 1 (007112) and Advanced Photography (007114). Music includes Campus Band (006023), Concert Band (006013), Cadet Band (006143, Troy High), Symphonic Band (006003), Jazz Ensemble (006033), Jazz Explorations (006042), Color Guard (006002), Percussion (006104), Freshman Orchestra (006083), Concert Orchestra (006073), Symphony Orchestra (006063), Philharmonic Orchestra (006093, Troy High), Treble Choir (006113), Concert Choir (006103), Mixed Chorus (006123, Athens), Madrigal Singers (006133, Athens), Chorus/Choir Accompanist (006132), AP Music Theory (006053), and Intro to Music Technology and Recording (006501) using ProTools. Theatre Arts are Theatre I, II and III (000402, 000412, 000422) and Youth Theatre (000162). Health (008852) is required for graduation, and Peer Mediation (008573) is a grade 12 course. Physical education includes Intro to Physical Activity Level 1 (007952) and Level 2 (007962), one of which is required for graduation; Exercise and Lifelong Fitness (006162), Self Defense (006172), Net Sports & Fitness (008082), Fall and Spring Team Sports & Fitness (007972, 007992), Weight Training and Aerobics fall and spring (007922, 007912), Tumbling & Gymnastics/Fitness (008042), Learning to Swim (007942), Lifeguarding/Advanced Swimming (008072, which requires students to be 15 years old and carries a $40 cost if Red Cross certification is desired), and Strength and Conditioning (008014). The President's Challenge Physical Fitness Test is given in most physical education classes.

Mathematics, Science and Social Studies. Math courses include Algebra 1 (003043), Intensified Algebra 1 (103123/203123), Geometry (003063), Geometry Honors (003930), Algebra 2 Part A and Part B (003263, 003273), Algebra 2 (003093), Algebra 2 Honors (003183), Precalculus (003233), Precalculus Honors (003253), College Algebra (003023, Troy High), Calculus AB AP (003173), Calculus BC AP (003203), Statistics AP (003213), and dual-enrollment Calculus 3 (003212) and Linear Algebra (003222) through Lawrence Tech. Computing courses are Computer Science 1 (003142, Troy High), AP Computer Science A (003162 at Troy High and 003163 at Athens), Computer Science Principles AP (003373), Cybersecurity (003172 at THS and 103172/203172 at AHS), and Introduction to Data Science (103383/203383), built on Python and referencing Google, NASA and Netflix. Science includes Introductory Biology (004003), Biology: Anatomy and Physiology (004053), Genetics, Bacteriology, Biotechnology, and Embryology (004063), Advanced Placement Biology (004073), Chemistry 1 and Chemistry 2, Chemistry 2 AP (004243), Organic Chemistry (004102), Introductory Physics (004213), Physics 1 (004223), Physics 2 (004233), Physics 2 AP (004253), Physics C AP (004263), Astronomy (004212), Forensic Science (004042), Environmental Science (004222) and Environmental Science AP (004273). Social studies spans World History/Geography 1 (002232), Human Geography AP (002503), American History/Geography 1 and 2 (102023, 202023) covering the United States from 1877, American History/Geography AP (002013), Economics (002062), Economics AP (002073), Government and Civics (002072), Government AP (002052), World History/Geography 2 (002242), World History/Geography AP (002233), Psychology 1 and 2 (002152, 002162 at Troy High), Psychology AP (002163), Sociology (002182), Mental Health (002112, Athens), Philosophy (002082, Athens), Comparative Government and Politics AP (002042) built around China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria and Russia, Political Science (002322), Human Rights and The Law (002102), History of American Criminal Law (002032), History through Film (002034), Conflicts of the 20th & 21st Centuries (002502, Athens), Introduction to Leadership (002122), Leadership Lab (002125) and LINK (002222).

Special Education and World Language. Special education courses, placed in collaboration with an IEP case manager and certified by an IEPT, include Achievement Skills 1A through 4B (109909/209909, 109910/209910, 109911/209911, 109912/209912), Linguistics 2D, 2E and 2F (009273, 009283, 009263), Reading Strategies (009201), Integrated Math 1 and 2 (003003, 003103), English Language Arts 1 and 2 (009303, 009573), Math Skills A/B (009332/009342) and Life Skills Math (009632/009642). World language sequences are French 1 through 4 and French AP (000603, 000613, 000623, 000633, 000643), Spanish 1 through 4 and Spanish AP (000693, 000703, 000713, 000723, 000733), Japanese 1 through 4 and Japanese AP (000823, 000833, 000843, 000863, 008863), Chinese 1 through 4 and Chinese AP (000853, 000873, 000883, 000893, 000813), and German 1 through 4 (000653, 000663, 000673, 000683). Proficiency targets are stated against the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, from Novice-mid/Novice-high at level 1 to Intermediate-high/Advanced-low at the AP level; Japanese 2 students read and write 120 basic Kanji characters, Japanese 3 adds another 170 or more, and Japanese 4 adds another 180 or more.

Oakland Schools Technical Campus. OSTC-Southeast is located at 5055 Delemere Street, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, on the Southeast Campus in Royal Oak, Michigan, with a Northeast Campus in Pontiac, Michigan. Programs are open to grades 11-12 on a selective basis; OSTC recommends high school credit based on local district requirements, generally 1.5 credits per semester. If regular students carry six credits, OSTC students must carry three credits at their home high school in addition to three credits at OSTC. Two sessions are offered, 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM; morning classes begin at 7:50 AM and are dismissed at 10:20 AM, and afternoon classes begin at 12:00 PM and are dismissed at 2:30 PM. Programs listed include Automotive Technology and Cosmetology (each must begin in 11th grade), Collision Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, and Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security). A bus transports students to OSTC-SE, though afternoon-session students must provide their own transportation home. Applications are made online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February, and the book warns athletes that credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved.

Antidiscrimination grievance procedure. Students or employees alleging discrimination on the basis of sex including sexual harassment, race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status, or handicap file a written grievance with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator. In Step 1 the grievance form goes to the immediate supervisor or administrator within 10 workdays of the incident; not later than the next workday a copy is sent to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services; within 5 workdays of filing the supervisor meets the grievant; and within 3 workdays of that meeting a written answer is given. In Step 2 the grievant appeals within 3 workdays of receiving the answer, the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services or Deputy Superintendent meets the grievant within 10 workdays of the appeal, and gives a written answer within 5 workdays of the meeting. In Step 3 the grievant appeals to the Superintendent within 3 workdays, the Superintendent meets within 10 workdays, and gives a written answer within 5 workdays; that decision is final and binding. A grievance not filed or appealed within the time limits is deemed abandoned, failure to hold a meeting or render a decision allows automatic appeal to the next level, time limits may be extended only by mutual written agreement, and records are treated confidentially with no record kept in a staff member's personnel file if the final decision finds no reasonable basis.
